verses.text: Then the Spirit led Jesus into the wilderness so the devil could test him.
He fasted forty days and forty nights. After all that, hunger finally hit.
The tempter came up and said, “If you’re God’s Son, tell these stones to become bread.”
Jesus answered, “Scripture says, ‘A person doesn’t live on bread alone, but on every word that comes from God’s mouth.’”
Then the devil took him to the holy city and set him on the highest point of the temple.
“If you’re God’s Son, jump down,” he said. “Scripture says, ‘He’ll command his angels about you,’ and, ‘They’ll carry you in their hands so you don’t strike your foot on a stone.’”
Jesus told him, “Scripture also says, ‘Don’t test the Lord your God.’”
Again the devil took him to a very high mountain and showed him every kingdom in the world and all their glory.
“I’ll give you all this,” he said, “if you bow down and worship me.”
Jesus said, “Get behind me, Satan! Scripture says, ‘Worship the Lord your God, and serve him only.’”
Then the devil left him, and angels came to serve him. 👼
When Jesus heard that John had been handed over, he went back to Galilee.
He left Nazareth and settled in Capernaum by the sea, in the regions of Zebulun and Naphtali.
That fulfilled what the prophet Isaiah had said:
“Land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali, the road by the sea, beyond the Jordan—Galilee of the Gentiles—
the people sitting in darkness saw a great light; on those sitting in death’s shadow, light has dawned.”
From then on, Jesus began preaching: “Turn back to God! Heaven’s Kingdom is close!”
Walking beside the Sea of Galilee, Jesus saw two brothers: Simon, also called Peter, and his brother Andrew. They were fishermen, casting a net into the sea. 🎣
He said to them, “Come follow me. I’ll teach you to fish for people.”
Right away, they left their nets and followed him.
Going on from there, he saw two more brothers: James, Zebedee’s son, and John his brother. They were in a boat with Zebedee their father, repairing their nets. Jesus called them.
At once they left the boat and their father, and followed him.
Jesus traveled all through Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, preaching the Good News of the Kingdom, and healing every disease and sickness among the people.

News about him spread through all Syria. People brought him everyone who was sick or suffering from diseases and severe pain, people tormented by demons, those having seizures, and those who couldn’t move. Jesus healed them.
Huge crowds followed him from Galilee, the Decapolis, Jerusalem, Judea, and across the Jordan.
